text: dev.sh format (biome format --write .) re-dirties opencode-context-watch.example.json and .github/.config.cjs on every run — HEAD is not biome-format-clean, so ./dev.sh all leaves the working tree dirty. Fix: add a biome.json with files.ignore or format-clean the two files at HEAD.

compact_context reports success but does nothing on opencode 1.18.11 — the v2 session.compact endpoint is a stub that RESOLVES (does not throw) with {error:{_tag:'ServiceUnavailableError',message:'Session compact is not available yet'}}, and the v1 session.command path also resolves with UnknownError 'Unexpected server error'; since compaction never runs, the experimental.compaction.autocontinue compactMessage feature cannot be observed live on this build

Starting an isolated OpenCode 2.0.16 background service on fazuh-id-3 with redirected XDG_CONFIG/DATA/STATE/CACHE plus 'opencode2 service start' hangs until timeout and never writes service.json; --standalone works but creates no service registration, so a plugin cannot discover the private server URL

Verifying plugin load with 'opencode2 api get /api/plugin --standalone' in a project returns an empty list until a session has booted that location; the local plugin only appears in a later server's run log, so the endpoint alone gives a false negative

Probing the OpenCode 2.0.16 plugin context: the V2 docs say ctx.model.list() returns Model.Info[] but the runtime returns {location,data}; ctx.session.compact is absent even though POST /api/session/{id}/compact exists, so a compact tool needs an undocumented authenticated service.json HTTP hack or must be dropped

Running the repo's own documented lint command 'bunx biome check .' > biome.json ignores .github/.config.cjs but not .github/scripts/, so the full-tree check fails on 3 pre-existing release-tooling findings in materialize-unreleased.cjs; lint only owned paths (src tests docs package.json) until the release-tooling work lands

Probing the opencode 2.0.16 context hook on fazuh-id-3 > session.step.ended is published AFTER the next step's context assembly, so a plugin caching usage from that event is always one model request behind (the first two requests of a session can never carry a context warning); also ctx.session.get({sessionID}).tokens is the same CUMULATIVE sum as session.usage.updated, not the per-step context size, and plugin console.log/console.error never appear in 'opencode2 run --print-logs' output
